description: Canonical feature contract shared by the BugDNA API and the Python risk service. Generated from backend/src/modules/analysis/features/registry.ts — edit that file, then run `npm run contracts:generate`. Do not edit this file by hand.

features.label: Lines added
features.description: Total added lines across the diff. Large additions introduce more new behaviour that has never run in production.

features.label: Lines deleted
features.description: Total removed lines. Deletions can remove guardrails as easily as dead code, so they are counted separately from additions.

features.label: Total churn
features.description: Added plus deleted lines — the overall size of the change, and the single strongest predictor of review difficulty.

features.label: Files changed
features.description: How many files the pull request touches. Wide changes are harder to review carefully and harder to revert cleanly.

features.label: Commits
features.description: Number of commits. Very high counts often indicate an unsquashed exploratory branch rather than a reviewed change.

features.label: Average change per file
features.description: Mean changed lines per file. Distinguishes a broad mechanical rename from a deep rewrite of a few files.

features.label: Largest single-file change
features.description: Churn in the most-modified file. A single very large file change concentrates risk in one place.

features.label: Deletion ratio
features.description: Share of churn that is deletions. A deletion-heavy change is more likely to remove behaviour something else depends on.

features.label: Files deleted
features.description: Files removed entirely. Deletions break importers and callers that the diff does not show.

features.label: Files renamed or moved
features.description: Renames and moves. They are usually safe but silently break dynamic imports, build config and documentation links.

features.label: Source files changed
features.description: Files classified as application source, excluding tests, docs and generated output.

features.label: Test files changed
features.description: Test files touched. Changing behaviour and its tests together is a strong signal the author considered the failure modes.

features.label: Includes test changes
features.description: Whether any test file is part of this change. A behavioural change with no test movement is the most common avoidable risk.

features.label: Test-to-source churn ratio
features.description: Test churn divided by source churn. Low values on a large change suggest the new behaviour is largely unverified.

features.label: Configuration files changed
features.description: Configuration changes take effect immediately on deploy and are rarely covered by tests.

features.label: Infrastructure files changed
features.description: Dockerfiles, CI workflows and deployment manifests. Failures here affect the deployment itself, not just the application.

features.label: Documentation-only change
features.description: Whether the change touches nothing but documentation. These carry effectively no deployment risk.

features.label: Generated files changed
features.description: Build output, lockfiles and generated code. Large diffs here inflate apparent size without adding reviewable logic.

features.label: Adds TODO or FIXME markers
features.description: New TODO/FIXME/HACK markers indicate the author knowingly left work unfinished in this change.

features.label: Dependency manifest changed
features.description: A package manifest or lockfile changed. Upgrades pull in third-party code that no reviewer on this PR has read.

features.label: Dependency files changed
features.description: How many manifests or lockfiles changed, across how many ecosystems.

features.label: Lockfile churn
features.description: Lines changed in lockfiles, a proxy for how much transitive dependency surface moved.

features.label: Database migrations changed
features.description: Schema migrations are among the hardest changes to roll back, because the data has already moved.

features.label: Contains destructive schema changes
features.description: The diff contains DROP, TRUNCATE, an unqualified DELETE, or a new NOT NULL without a default — operations that can lose data or fail on a populated table.

features.label: Changes a public API surface
features.description: An exported symbol or route handler changed. Callers outside this pull request may depend on the old shape.

features.label: Files with public API changes
features.description: How many files changed an exported or externally routed symbol.

features.label: Modules touched
features.description: Distinct modules or components the change spans. A change crossing many modules is harder to reason about and to revert.

features.label: Spans multiple modules
features.description: Whether the change crosses module boundaries rather than staying local.

features.label: Largest module share of churn
features.description: Share of churn in the single most-affected module. High concentration means focused work; low means the change is diffuse.

features.label: Languages touched
features.description: Number of distinct languages in the diff. Multi-language changes need reviewers who may not overlap.

features.label: Touches authentication or secrets
features.description: Paths or diff content referencing auth, permissions, tokens or cryptography. Mistakes here fail silently and expose data.

features.label: Removes error handling
features.description: The diff deletes a try/catch, except or error branch. Removing a guard converts a handled failure into an outage.

features.label: Has a description
features.description: Whether the author explained the change. An unexplained PR is reviewed less effectively, whatever its size.

features.label: Description length
features.description: Characters of PR description, as a rough proxy for how much context reviewers were given.

features.label: Review comments
features.description: Inline review comments so far. Zero on a large change means nobody has examined the code yet.

features.label: Draft pull request
features.description: Draft PRs are not merge candidates yet, so their risk is informational.

features.label: Pull request age
features.description: Hours since the PR was opened. Long-lived branches drift further from the base and merge less predictably.

features.label: Repository median PR size (30d)
features.description: Typical PR size in this repository recently. It is the baseline this PR's size is judged against — 400 lines is unremarkable in some repos and an outlier in others.

features.label: Size relative to repository norm
features.description: This PR's churn divided by the repository's recent median. Values well above 1 mean the change is unusually large for this codebase.

features.label: Repository deployment failure rate (90d)
features.description: Share of recorded deployments that failed or were rolled back. A repository that ships badly is riskier to ship to.

features.label: Incident history of touched modules
features.description: Share of past reported incidents whose pull requests touched at least one of the same modules. This is the clearest historical signal BugDNA has, because it comes from outcomes a human confirmed.

features.label: Author pull requests here (90d)
features.description: How many PRs this author has opened in this repository recently — a proxy for familiarity with the codebase.

features.label: Author familiarity with touched modules
features.description: Share of the modules in this PR that the author has changed before. Editing unfamiliar code is a well-understood source of defects.
